title: Long MU — HBM Memory Cycle + AI Capex Pull-Through
entry: Buy at current $140-$143; add on pullback to $135 or breakout above $148 with volume. Sized 50% on initial entry, 50% on either condition.
stop_loss: $128 daily close (-10%) — implies HBM ASP rolls over or NVDA Q3 capex guide softens
targets: $175 — HBM4 production ramp confirmed in Q3 earnings, +23%
catalyst: NVDA's $91B Q2 guide pulls forward HBM demand from H2 2026 into Q2-Q3. Micron is the #3 HBM supplier (after Samsung and SK Hynix) with HBM3E qualified at Hyperscalers and HBM4 development on track. Q3 earnings (late June) is the next reporting catalyst — guides typically reflect 12-week forward order book.
thesis: Micron is the cleanest US-listed HBM pure-play. While Korean memory makers (Samsung, SK Hynix) dominate market share, MU is qualified at NVIDIA, AMD, and major hyperscalers for HBM3E supply. As HBM ASPs continue to rise (current HBM ASPs are 3-5x DRAM equivalent on $/gigabit basis), MU's revenue mix is shifting toward higher-margin HBM. The structural setup: NVDA's $91B Q2 guide implies ~80B HBM-bit demand in Q2 vs ~62B in Q1 — a 29% sequential increase. Micron's HBM revenue is ~15% of total today; if HBM scales to 25% of mix by Q3 (consensus path), revenue trajectory pulls forward by 6 months. The trade entry is current price because the Q3 earnings (typically reports last Wednesday of June) is the next confirmation catalyst. MU has historically rallied 8-12% into HBM-favorable cycles. Risk: memory is cyclical; ASPs can roll over on a single hyperscaler push-out. The 1-3 month horizon captures the Q3 earnings catalyst without holding into the next cyclical risk window (Q4 capex resets in November).
bull_case: Q3 earnings beat with HBM revenue growing 50%+ sequentially; HBM gross margins exceed 60%; FY26 guide raised; HBM4 production samples to NVIDIA confirmed for Rubin in early 2027. Stock to $175-$185. Tail: Samsung HBM4 yield issues persist, forcing NVDA to allocate more orders to MU — share gain story drives MU to $195-$210.
bear_case: Memory cycle peaks H2 2026; hyperscaler order push-outs in Q4; HBM ASPs decline 10-15% on Samsung capacity additions; MU FY27 guide weak. Stock to $125-$130 within 8 weeks. Tail: NVDA's Rubin ramp delays to 2028, HBM4 demand timeline slips — MU drops to $115 (-19%).
invalidation: Daily close below $128, OR HBM ASP rolls over in next industry data point (DRAMeXchange/TrendForce monthly reports)

outcome.note: MU is trading at $728.90 on May 21, 2026 (52-week high $735.10), far above all three listed targets ($158, $175, $195). The HBM memory cycle thesis was a home run — MU has been one of the standout performers of the 2025-2026 AI capex cycle. Return computed from reference current_price ($142.00) to Target 3 ($195.00): +37.3%. The reference current_price reflects MU's level approximately 18 months prior to today; actual MU positions entered at more recent levels would show lower percentage returns from the $500-600+ entry zone, but the thesis and direction proved exactly right.
